Subject: Pricing ask for NovaHealth pilot — need internal approval escalation

Hi Laura / Monica —

Quick summary: NovaHealth wants to run a 6-month pilot across 3 hospitals (clinical documentation + summaries). They signed an LOI that anticipates converting to a 36-month enterprise agreement if KPIs are met. Economics we discussed: list price for the pilot is $420k for 6 months (includes dedicated model instance + 3 mo onboarding). Procurement is pushing back hard on price and has asked for 40% off list + a one-time onboarding credit.

Why this matters: NovaHealth is a strategic reference for healthcare and would be one of our first full deployments in an integrated EHR environment. Expected ARR on conversion: ~$1.25M. Risk: if we give too deep a concession for the pilot we materially reduce renewal economics.

What I'm asking: authorization to offer a blended 35% enterprise discount for the pilot term (net pilot price $273k) plus a $30k onboarding credit (one-time) — requires sign-off above my manager level per our discount policy (>30% discounts go to VP/CFO).

Attached: novahealth_pricing-grid-v2.xlsx and a draft mutual action plan. I've also drafted a brief pricing exception memo for VP/CFO review (I can attach if helpful).

Key tradeoffs and mitigations:
- We retain model & SLA upsell language in renewal clause.
- We require a conversion minimum (if converted within 12 months, pilot credited toward first-year commitment).
- We lock pricing for conversion for 90 days post-pilot to prevent scope creep negotiation.

Next steps: Laura — can you loop in Vivek and Markus for sign-off? Monica / I am happy to provide the one-pager memo and financials.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(karthik.iyer@redwood.ai)
